submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness delivers the best possible pion/kaon separation performance at 10 GeV/c with 4.649 sigma separation. This represents a 19.4% improvement over the second-best option (R1 at 2 cm: 3.893 sigma) and a 64.8% improvement over R2 (at 4 cm: 2.822 sigma). 

The recommendation is based on comprehensive simulation results across all three radiator candidates at six thickness values (18 total configurations). R3 consistently outperformed both alternatives across all thicknesses tested, demonstrating its superior optical properties for Cherenkov detection.

All hard constraints are satisfied: the radiator is from the approved candidate list, thickness is within the 1-6 cm range, and no ageing test data indicates transparency loss exceeding 10%. While R3 is a porous material without explicitly mentioned hydrophobic treatment (presenting medium ageing risk compared to R1's low risk), the absence of actual failing ageing data combined with the substantial performance advantage justifies this selection to achieve the stated goal of "best possible" separation.

R3 also shows robust performance across the 1-4 cm range (>4.3 sigma), providing tolerance to manufacturing variations. This configuration directly fulfills the primary project objective while meeting all technical requirements.
